## Today's Agenda

::: {.callout-tip title="Exercise"}
You will do a **mini version** of a **small part** of the group project, from questioning to exploration, in about 60 minutes of the class.
:::

::: {.callout-caution title="Expectations"}
You are **not** expected to know everything yet. 

- This is only for practice, and it counts for our weekly participation.

- My goal is for you all to attempt creating your own plots. I genuinely don't care if you can create a stellar plot and/or analysis with time constraints. 

- I care more about your effort and creativity! Surprise me!

:::

## The tentative deadlines

| Checkpoint | What it is |
|---|---|
| 1. Project proposal | Research question and data choice |
| 2. EDA report | What is the data telling you? |
| 3. Peer review | Give feedback on another team's report |
| 4. Final report | Your full-complete analysis |

*Details and rubric will be released soon.*



## Today's Participation Credit

1. Get into groups and set up.
2. Read the data description and come up with *two interesting questions*.
3. Make two plots to explore them.
4. Propose *one new variable* for your analysis.
5. Knit into a *pdf* and submit to Gradescope.
6. **If you are done early, come up and show me your results before you go.**


## Meet the data: 

::: {.callout-tip title="Survey Results"}
A survey of university students about their sleep and study habits.
:::

::: {.callout-warning title="Disclaimer"}
**The data is totally simulated** for this class. Don't treat the findings as real facts about students or sleep. I have nothing do with all the claims that you might make about these students!
:::

Each row is *one student*. Each column is *one variable*.


## Data description (i){.smaller}

| Variable | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `program` | Categorical | Arts, Business, Science, Health Sci, Engineering |
| `num_courses` | Numeric (count) | Courses this term (3 to 6) |
| `study_hours_week` | Numeric | Average study hours per week |
| `sleep_hours` | Numeric | Average hours of sleep per night |
| `favourite_drink` | Categorical | Coffee, Tea, Energy drink, Pop, Water |


## Data description (ii){.smaller}

| Variable | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `has_early_class` | Binary | Any 8:30 am class? (Yes / No) |
| `work_hours_week` | Numeric | Paid work hours per week (0 = no job) |
| `stress_level` | Ordinal (1-5) | Self-rated stress (1 = low, 5 = high) |
| `sleep_quality` | Ordinal (1-5) | Self-rated sleep quality (1 = poor, 5 = great) |
| `avg_grade` | Numeric | Average grade (%) |





## Two kinds of questions

::: {.callout-note title="Task"}
I want you to generate two questions for this mini-project.
:::

::: {.callout-important title="Numeric x Numeric"}
Choices of numeric variables: *number of courses*, *number of study hours per week*, *average hours of sleep per night*, *number of work hours per week*, and *average grades*.
:::

::: {.callout-caution title="Numeric x Categorical"}
Choices of categorical variables: *program type*, *favourite drinks*, *early classes?*, *stress level*, and *sleep quality*.
:::


## Numeric x Numeric

::: {.callout-note title="Purpose"}
Is one number related to another?
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Plots"}
E.g. scatterplots, jitter, `geom_smooth`, colouring points by a categorical variable (`aes(colour = ...)`), etc.

Example: *"Is the relationship between sleep hours and average grades the same across programs?"*
:::

## Example plot


::: {.cell}
::: {.cell-output-display}
![](DATA100-F26-Group-Project-Guidance-1_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-2-1.png){width=672}
:::
:::


*Does the pattern look the same in every program?*


## Numeric x Categorical

::: {.callout-note title="Purpose"}
Does a number differ across groups?
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Plots"}
E.g. boxplots, bar plots, histograms with facet grids, etc.

Example: *"How does the distribution of weekly study hours differ across programs?"*
:::

## Example plot


::: {.cell}
::: {.cell-output-display}
![](DATA100-F26-Group-Project-Guidance-1_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-3-1.png){width=672}
:::
:::


*How do the centre and spread differ across programs?*


## Weak vs. strong questions

::: {.callout-caution title="Weak Questions"}
A weak question is vague. It doesn't say which variables to use, what to compare, or what a plot or table would show. 

- *Is sleep related to anything?*

- *Analyze and see which undergraduate program is the best.*

:::


::: {.callout-tip title="Strong Questions"}
A strong question is specific enough that the reader could make the plot without asking you anything.

- *Do students with more courses study more hours per week?*

- *Does average stress level of students differ by their program?*

:::



## Careful with your wording

| Instead of | Try |
|---|---|
| "Energy drinks **cause** less sleep." | "Energy drink drinkers **tend to sleep less**." |
| "Working **makes** students study less." | "More work hours is **associated with** fewer study hours." |

Data like this shows **patterns**, not **proof of cause**.


## Getting started

::: {.callout-note title="Groups"}
Form a group with your neighbours. Maximum group of four.
:::

1. Download `sleep_survey.csv` and `mini_project_template.Rmd` from the *MyLearningSpace*
2. Put them in the *same folder*, then open the *.Rmd* in *RStudio*.


## Step 1: Write two questions

Read the data description in the lecture slides, then fill in **Part 1** of the Rmd:

1. One **numeric × numeric** question
2. One **categorical × numeric** question

Name your variables and say what you'd compare.


## Step 2: Plots

1 (numeric × numeric) and 1 (categorical × numeric)

- Make a **scatterplot** for your first question
- Add appropriate axis labels 
- Write **2 to 3 sentences** on what you observe for each plot


## Step 3: One new variable

What **one variable** could you add to this survey that would make the analysis **more interesting**?


- Explain what it would let you ask or change how you read an existing pattern.

  - *A variable that changes how you read a pattern beats just another column.*

- **Example:** `year_of_study`. Upper-year students might both study more *and* earn higher grades, so year could change how we read the study hours vs. grades pattern.



## Wrap-up and submit

1. **Knit** your Rmd to PDF
2. **Upload** the PDF to Gradescope *(one per group, add all members)*
3. Unfinished is okay. Submit what you have.


::: {.callout-note title="Next Project Guidance"}
Tuesday, November 10. More details will come!
:::

::: {.callout-warning title="Homework for Reading Week"}
Make a group of 4-5 students among yourselves. Think about the type of data that you want to work with for your final project.
:::

<script>
  // htmlwidgets need to know to resize themselves when slides are shown/hidden.
  // Fire the "slideenter" event (handled by htmlwidgets.js) when the current
  // slide changes (different for each slide format).
  (function () {
    // dispatch for htmlwidgets
    function fireSlideEnter() {
      const event = window.document.createEvent("Event");
      event.initEvent("slideenter", true, true);
      window.document.dispatchEvent(event);
    }

    function fireSlideChanged(previousSlide, currentSlide) {
      fireSlideEnter();

      // dispatch for shiny
      if (window.jQuery) {
        if (previousSlide) {
          window.jQuery(previousSlide).trigger("hidden");
        }
        if (currentSlide) {
          window.jQuery(currentSlide).trigger("shown");
        }
      }
    }

    // hookup for slidy
    if (window.w3c_slidy) {
      window.w3c_slidy.add_observer(function (slide_num) {
        // slide_num starts at position 1
        fireSlideChanged(null, w3c_slidy.slides[slide_num - 1]);
      });
    }

  })();
</script>
